catalog-0122.look: Observe the central parting of her hair and the gentle contours of her face, comparing her expression with other goddess statues nearby. Even a slight shift in your viewing angle subtly alters the direction of her gaze.

catalog-0123.title: The Vienne Venus
catalog-0123.author: Ancient Roman Sculptor
catalog-0123.background: This ancient statue portrays Aphrodite crouching, giving the goddess an unexpected sense of intimacy and startled vulnerability. The motif proved immensely popular and was widely replicated throughout antiquity.
catalog-0123.look: Trace the rhythmic loop formed by her bent knees and arms, and step around to view the sweeping curves of her back. You will immediately sense how different this pose feels from standing statues of Venus.

catalog-0124.title: The Borghese Ares
catalog-0124.author: Ancient Roman Sculptor
catalog-0124.background: Depicting the god of war, this ancient sculpture comes from the renowned Borghese collection acquired by Napoleon. Rather than showing the deity in the heat of battle, the sculptor presents him in a composed, contemplative stance.
catalog-0124.look: Study his helmet alongside the relaxed alignment of his body, contrasting his emblems of war with his calm expression. Notice how the sense of weight shifts when viewed from the front versus the side.

catalog-0125.title: Hermes Unfastening His Sandal
catalog-0125.author: Ancient Roman Sculptor
catalog-0125.background: Hermes, the swift messenger of the gods, bends down to reach for his sandal. Showing the fleet-footed deity just before or after a journey introduces a candid, everyday gesture into classical sculpture.
catalog-0125.look: Notice the interplay between his outstretched hand and raised foot, and how the leaning figure maintains effortless equilibrium. Follow the turn of his head to imagine what he is about to do next.

catalog-0126.title: The Mattei Athena
catalog-0126.author: Ancient Roman Sculptor
catalog-0126.background: Representing Athena, goddess of wisdom and warfare, this sculpture follows a classical Greek prototype. Her drapery and armor work together to express her dual divine roles.
catalog-0126.look: Spot the helmet resting on her head and the attributes adorning her chest, then follow how the folds of her garment reveal the stance beneath. Contrast her martial gear with the quiet serenity of her face.

catalog-0127.title: The Pallas of Velletri
catalog-0127.author: Ancient Roman Sculptor
catalog-0127.background: Known as Pallas—another name for Athena—this imposing statue conveys the majesty of an ancient cult image. Its present appearance reflects historical restorations added in later centuries.
catalog-0127.look: Step back first to take in the statue's commanding height, admiring the balanced geometry of her features and drapery. Then move closer to see if you can trace the seams of later restorations.

catalog-0128.title: Torso of the Diadoumenos Type
catalog-0128.author: Ancient Roman Sculptor
catalog-0128.background: This fragment follows the famous Greek type of a victorious athlete tying a victory ribbon around his head. Even incomplete, it preserves the classical harmony of the human figure and invites the viewer to imagine the missing limbs.
catalog-0128.look: Observe the subtle counter-tilt between the shoulders and hips, and visualize how the body's weight once rested on a single leg. Follow the rippling play of muscle across the marble surface.

catalog-0129.title: Statue of Horus (formerly Posno Collection)
catalog-0129.author: Ancient Egyptian Sculptor
catalog-0129.background: This sculpture depicts the god Horus in the form of a falcon. Revered as the divine protector of kingship, the god's formidable power is distilled into this animal form.
catalog-0129.look: Look closely at the sharp beak and piercing eyes, then follow the sweeping lines of the folded wings wrapping around the body. Compare the statue's presence from the front and in profile.

catalog-0130.title: Outer Coffin of Tamutnefert
catalog-0130.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0130.background: Crafted to protect the deceased, this painted wooden coffin is covered with faces and divine imagery expressing hopes for eternal life. In ancient Egypt, the coffin itself was conceived as a new body for the departed.
catalog-0130.look: Move your gaze from the painted face down across the richly patterned chest, picking out both the hieroglyphic inscriptions and the figures of protective deities. Pay special attention to the areas where vibrant pigments still survive.

catalog-0131.title: Coffin of Lady Madja
catalog-0131.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0131.background: This richly decorated coffin was fashioned for a woman named Madja, bearing her name alongside protective sacred motifs. Here, an essential funerary vessel also stands as a remarkable work of art.
catalog-0131.look: Examine the sculpted contours of the face and the scenes covering the body, tracing the crisp divisions between fields of color. Notice how the hieroglyphs are woven seamlessly into the overall decoration.

catalog-0132.title: Mummy of a Man Wrapped in Cartonnage
catalog-0132.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0132.background: This funerary ensemble consists of a body wrapped in linen and encased in decorative cartonnage, reflecting Egyptian beliefs in preserving the physical form for the afterlife. Details of the individual's name and exact date can be checked in the gallery documentation.
catalog-0132.look: Observe how the wrappings carefully follow the contours of the human body, and compare the decoration on the face with that across the chest. Rather than guessing what lies beneath, focus on reading the symbolic imagery across the surface.

catalog-0133.title: The Gebel el-Arak Knife
catalog-0133.author: Predynastic Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0133.background: Created before the unification of Egypt, this ceremonial dagger pairs a finely worked blade with a handle of contrasting material. Its carved grip is packed with scenes of animals and fierce combat.
catalog-0133.look: Look closely at the miniature figures and animals carved into the handle, and compare the imagery on both sides. Notice how the extraordinary craftsmanship elevates this object far beyond an ordinary weapon.

catalog-0134.title: Stele of the Serpent King (Djet)
catalog-0134.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0134.background: This stone stele commemorates an Early Dynastic pharaoh, using royal emblems that shed light on the earliest stages of Egyptian writing. With striking economy of form, it proclaims the ruler's enduring presence.
catalog-0134.look: Find the serpent carved inside the rectangular frame and notice its relationship to the falcon perched above. This clean, spare composition shows how a royal name was recorded with just a few bold lines.

catalog-0135.title: Stele of Princess Nefertiabet
catalog-0135.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0135.background: This funerary stele was made for an Old Kingdom princess. Detailed depictions of food and ritual offerings express the wish to guarantee her perpetual sustenance in the afterlife.
catalog-0135.look: Look at the seated princess facing the offering table before her, and try to identify the various delicacies laid out. Notice the harmonious grid uniting images and hieroglyphs.

catalog-0136.title: Statue of an Amarna Princess
catalog-0136.author: Ancient Egyptian Sculptor
catalog-0136.background: Representing a young princess from the family of Pharaoh Akhenaten, this sculpture displays the supple, naturalistic style characteristic of the Amarna period. Its gentle forms evoke an intimate glimpse of royal family life.
catalog-0136.look: Examine the distinctive shape of the head and neck, comparing them with traditional statues of adult rulers. Notice the tender, childlike softness of her posture.

catalog-0137.title: Relief of Akhenaten and Nefertiti
catalog-0137.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0137.background: This carved relief portrays King Akhenaten and Queen Nefertiti during Egypt's religious revolution. Although the scene feels deeply personal, the royal couple's image carried profound theological significance.
catalog-0137.look: Observe the orientation of the two profiles and look for the rays of light and divine symbols descending from above. Notice how the shallow carving gives crisp clarity to every line.

catalog-0138.title: Vessel of General Djehuty
catalog-0138.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0138.background: Associated with a high-ranking general, this ancient Egyptian vessel showcases the sophisticated craftsmanship reserved for royalty and top officials. Even a functional form becomes a vehicle for prestige and authority.
catalog-0138.look: Follow the clean curve from the rim down through the body of the vessel, and search for the engraved inscriptions and motifs. Picture how it would have felt held in the hands.

catalog-0139.title: The Goddess Hathor Welcoming Seti I
catalog-0139.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0139.background: Taken from a royal tomb, this relief depicts the goddess Hathor greeting Pharaoh Seti I. The encounter affirms that divine protection follows the king into the afterlife, rendered in crisp, balanced linework.
catalog-0139.look: Focus on the space where their hands nearly meet, and compare the royal crown with the goddess's headdress and emblems. Admire the clean, crisp outlines of the low relief.

catalog-0140.title: Stele of the Young Ramesses II
catalog-0140.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0140.background: This stele presents Ramesses II in youthful form, weaving image and inscription together to proclaim the king's name. Even in childhood, royal authority is visibly entrusted to him.
catalog-0140.look: Look closely at the small figure amid the surrounding hieroglyphs and see how visual symbols combine to spell out the pharaoh's name. Notice the deliberate contrast in scale between the figures.

catalog-0141.title: Offering Statue of King Taharqa
catalog-0141.author: Ancient Egyptian Sculptor
catalog-0141.background: King Taharqa is shown presenting jars of wine to the falcon god Hemen. This ritual scene bridges ruler and deity while blending the heritage of the Kushite dynasty with enduring Egyptian tradition.
catalog-0141.look: Notice the king's hands offering the sacred vessels and follow the alignment between ruler and god. Look closely at the fine details of the royal kilt and crowns.

catalog-0142.title: Stele of Lady Taperet
catalog-0142.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0142.background: Created for a private woman, this funerary stele conveys prayers to the gods through vibrant color and script. It reminds us that hopes for the afterlife were cherished by ordinary individuals as well as royalty.
catalog-0142.look: Start at the curved top of the stele and work down to the figures below, seeking out the painted imagery that still survives. Notice how the lines of hieroglyphs neatly frame the scene.

catalog-0143.title: Statue of Ahmose-Nefertari
catalog-0143.author: Ancient Egyptian Artisan
catalog-0143.background: This statue portrays Queen Ahmose-Nefertari as she was revered after death—elevated to divine status and venerated as patroness of the royal tomb builders. It reflects the enduring memory of Egypt's influential queens.
catalog-0143.look: Examine her headdress and serene face, and look for the sacred attributes she holds that signal her deification. Consider how the sculpture unites her earthly role as queen with her status as a goddess.

catalog-0144.title: Pectoral Inscribed with the Name of Ramesses II
catalog-0144.author: Ancient Egyptian Goldsmith
catalog-0144.background: Inscribed with the pharaoh's royal name, this ornate pectoral demonstrates how royal authority was woven even into personal adornment. Within a compact scale, it concentrates extraordinary technical mastery.
catalog-0144.look: Look at the central royal cartouche and the crisp symmetry flanking it on either side. Notice the contrasting colors of the inlaid materials, and imagine how striking this jewel would have looked when worn.

catalog-0145.title: Statuette of the Cat Goddess Bastet
catalog-0145.author: Ancient Egyptian artisan
catalog-0145.background: This is the goddess Bastet, depicted in the form of a cat. She was worshipped as a protector of the home and family. It is also an engaging small-scale work as an animal sculpture.
catalog-0145.look: Look closely at the shape of the ears and eyes. Notice the quiet poise of her seated posture, and look for the ornament around her neck.

catalog-0146.title: Ostracon Depicting the Head of a King
catalog-0146.author: Ancient Egyptian draftsman
catalog-0146.background: This is a study of a king's head drawn on a flake of stone or pottery shard. Unlike a finished monument, it reveals the working process behind the scenes, letting us feel the artist's hand up close.
catalog-0146.look: Observe the contour of the face and the line of the eye. Look for places where the strokes were traced over again and again—a small fragment like this once led to grand wall paintings.

catalog-0147.title: Pendant with the Triad of Osorkon II
catalog-0147.author: Ancient Egyptian goldsmith
catalog-0147.background: This piece of jewelry brings together the gods Osiris, Isis, and Horus, and is associated with the name of King Osorkon II. It links the myth of the divine family with the legitimacy of the king.
catalog-0147.look: Count the three deities in the center and on either side, and admire the fine outlines in gold. Even at a size meant to be worn, the piece tells a grand mythic story.

catalog-0148.title: Statue of Sekhmet Guarding the Queen's Tomb
catalog-0148.author: Ancient Egyptian sculptor
catalog-0148.background: This statue depicts Sekhmet, the lion-headed goddess whose fierce power could bring both protection and danger. It is one of many such statues placed in repeating rows within temple precincts.
catalog-0148.look: Compare the human body with the lioness face, and look for the sun disk on her head and the emblem she holds. Beneath this calm posture lies immense power.

catalog-0149.title: Carved Waterfowl Vessel
catalog-0149.author: Ancient Egyptian artisan
catalog-0149.background: This vessel is fashioned in the shape of a waterfowl. Keen observation of animals was channeled directly into craftsmanship, bringing natural forms even into everyday objects.
catalog-0149.look: Follow the curve of the beak and body, and spot the opening that turns it into a container. Notice how lifelike bird anatomy is balanced with practical design.

catalog-0150.title: Mughal Horse-Head Dagger
catalog-0150.author: Mughal artisan
catalog-0150.background: This lavish dagger features a hilt carved in the form of a horse's head. Its jade and precious stones reflect the refined taste of courtly elites, uniting weaponry and jewelry in a single object.
catalog-0150.look: Examine the carving of the horse's ears and nostrils, and contrast the color of the stone with the metal blade. Imagine how it would be oriented when held in the hand.

catalog-0151.title: Tile Panel with a Poetry Competition
catalog-0151.author: Iranian potter
catalog-0151.background: This vibrantly colored tiled wall panel showcases the courtly culture of Iran. It depicts two figures competing in poetry in a garden, formed by 63 ceramic tiles fitting together into a single picture.
catalog-0151.look: Find the two figures and the garden plants, and let your eye trace the joints between the tiles. The blues and greens convey the lushness of the setting.

catalog-0152.title: Head of a Prince
catalog-0152.author: Islamic world artisan
catalog-0152.background: This sculptural head represents a royal figure. Its portrait-like features evoke courtly culture and remind us that Islamic art encompasses rich traditions of figurative sculpture.
catalog-0152.look: Notice the shape of the crown and hair, and compare the rendering of the eyes and mouth. From what survives, you can imagine the full figure it once belonged to.

catalog-0153.title: Ewer with Confronted Birds
catalog-0153.author: Islamic world metalworker
catalog-0153.background: This metal ewer incorporates a pair of birds into its design, adding animal motifs to a utilitarian vessel. Even the handle and spout become integral parts of the decoration.
catalog-0153.look: Find the two birds facing one another, and trace where the water pours and where the hand grips the handle. Follow the patterns wrapping smoothly around the curved surface.

catalog-0154.title: Duck Candlestick
catalog-0154.author: Islamic world metalworker
catalog-0154.background: This metal candlestick is adorned with the figure of a duck. A playful spirit animates an everyday lighting implement, uniting fine metalwork with expressive animal form.
catalog-0154.look: Look at the duck's silhouette and where the candle would be set. Trace the delicate engraved patterns up close, and picture the piece glowing with a lit flame.

catalog-0155.title: Mosque Lamp Inscribed with the Name of a Qalawunid Sultan
catalog-0155.author: Mamluk glassmaker
catalog-0155.background: This glass mosque lamp bears the name of a sultan. Its colors and calligraphy adorned sacred spaces, investing a luminous material with royal authority.
catalog-0155.look: Read the band of inscription around the body and spot the loops used to suspend the lamp. Imagine how the colors would glow with an oil wick burning inside.

catalog-0156.title: Reader in a Patchwork Robe
catalog-0156.author: Islamic world illuminator
catalog-0156.background: This miniature painting opens a manuscript. The figure's distinctive garment immediately draws the eye, packing narrative and ornament onto a small sheet of paper.
catalog-0156.look: Notice the shifting colors of the patchwork robe, and follow the reader's gaze toward the book. Be sure to take in the surrounding margins and decorative borders as well.

catalog-0157.title: Dish with a Peacock
catalog-0157.author: Islamic world potter
catalog-0157.background: This ceramic dish features a peacock at its center, with the bird's form adapted gracefully to the circular frame. It invites us to enjoy the interplay between functional tableware and decorative art.
catalog-0157.look: Focus on the bird in the middle and follow how its tail feathers echo the curve of the rim. Pay attention to the subtle variations in the glaze as well.

catalog-0158.title: Bookbinding Depicting a Prince's Outdoor Pastime
catalog-0158.author: Islamic world artisan
catalog-0158.background: This book cover portrays courtly leisure in nature. Here, the binding designed to protect the pages is a work of art in its own right, with figures and foliage starting a story before the reader even opens the book.
catalog-0158.look: Look at the central figure and the surrounding landscape, and spot the symmetrical ornamental details. You can sense the richness of the manuscript from its exterior alone.

catalog-0159.title: Beaker with Polo Players
catalog-0159.author: Islamic world glassmaker
catalog-0159.background: This drinking beaker is decorated with scenes of mounted polo players. It brings a favorite courtly sport onto a vessel for refreshments, capturing lively motion on a small curved surface.
catalog-0159.look: Search for the horses and the ball, and see how the riders are arranged around the curve of the glass. Take note of the areas where the original colored enamel still survives.

catalog-0160.title: Bowl with a Standard-Bearer
catalog-0160.author: Islamic world potter
catalog-0160.background: A figure holding a banner is painted across this ceramic bowl. The center of the vessel becomes a miniature stage, with imagery evocative of medieval courts and ceremonies.
catalog-0160.look: Examine the figure's banner and robe, and observe how the rim decoration frames the central scene. The composition is designed to be viewed from above.

catalog-0161.title: Two Attendants Carrying a Stool
catalog-0161.author: Ancient Assyrian artisan
catalog-0161.background: This relief once decorated the palace of King Sargon II. Depicting attendants carrying furniture, it offers a glimpse into daily court life and draws attention to the people who upheld royal grandeur.
catalog-0161.look: Look at the two men's hands and the legs of the stool, and compare their synchronized stride. The lines of their garments convey a clear sense of forward motion.

catalog-0162.title: Sargon II and a High Official
catalog-0162.author: Ancient Assyrian artisan
catalog-0162.background: In this palace relief, the king stands side by side with a high-ranking official. Differences in stature and dress signify social rank, carving the political hierarchy of the royal court into stone.
catalog-0162.look: Compare the heights and headdresses of the two figures, and follow the gestures of their hands. Notice also the rhythmic, stylized lines of their beards and robes.

catalog-0163.title: Winged Genie Giving a Blessing
catalog-0163.author: Ancient Assyrian artisan
catalog-0163.background: This winged guardian spirit was carved to protect the king and the palace walls. Combining human and avian features, its composite form embodies supernatural power.
catalog-0163.look: Examine the individual feathers of the wings, and look closely at the ritual objects held in its hands. Its placement was directly tied to guarding the palace doorways.

catalog-0164.title: Attendants Carrying the King's Wheeled Throne
catalog-0164.author: Ancient Assyrian artisan
catalog-0164.background: This relief shows attendants moving a heavy royal throne. Royal authority depended on the labor of many hands, and the scene vividly documents preparations for court ceremony.
catalog-0164.look: Inspect the structure of the wheels and the throne, and count how many figures are hauling it. Their stance and footsteps convey the sheer weight of the load.

catalog-0165.title: Plaque of King Esarhaddon and Queen Mother Naqi'a
catalog-0165.author: Ancient Assyrian artisan
catalog-0165.background: This small plaque depicts and names the king alongside his mother, reflecting the vital political role of royal family ties. It expresses dynastic authority in a format very different from monumental palace reliefs.
catalog-0165.look: Observe the arrangement of the two figures and their inscriptions, and pay attention to the shape of the border. Small objects like this add crucial detail to dynastic history.

catalog-0166.title: Transporting Timber from Lebanon
catalog-0166.author: Ancient Assyrian artisan
catalog-0166.background: This scene shows timber being transported for palace construction, as prized Lebanese cedar was brought back to the Assyrian capital. Like a stone mural, it chronicles the king's vast building campaigns.
catalog-0166.look: Find the boats and the logs, and trace how the workers divide their tasks. You can easily imagine the long journey of these building materials.

catalog-0167.title: The Mesha Stele
catalog-0167.author: Ancient Moabite artisan
catalog-0167.background: This stele records the deeds of Mesha, king of Moab. It is a major surviving written monument of the ancient Levant, commissioned by the king to preserve his achievements for posterity.
catalog-0167.look: Follow the neat horizontal lines of script across the stone, taking note of the fractured and missing sections. Reading the stone itself becomes a direct way to uncover history.

catalog-0168.title: Temple-Shaped Architectural Model
catalog-0168.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0168.background: This small model represents a temple in miniature architectural form. It offers valuable clues to the appearance of lost sanctuaries, scaling down a sacred building into a portable object.
catalog-0168.look: Examine the shape of the doorway and roof, and look for decorative details along the walls. From these proportions, you can picture the scale of the full-sized temple.

catalog-0169.title: Sphinx-Shaped Furniture Ornament
catalog-0169.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0169.background: This furniture fitting takes the form of a composite human-and-animal figure. Characteristic of the eastern Mediterranean where artistic traditions intersected, it imbued even household furnishings with a protective presence.
catalog-0169.look: Look at the transition between the face and the animal body, and consider where it would have been mounted. This small carving reveals influences from multiple cultures.

catalog-0170.title: Seated Deity in a Wide-Hemmed Robe
catalog-0170.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0170.background: This statuette portrays an enthroned god whose broad, flaring garment marks elevated status. It provides important evidence for religious imagery in the ancient Levant.
catalog-0170.look: Notice the wide hem of the robe and the seated posture, and look at the positioning of the hands. Viewed head-on, the figure radiates quiet authority.

catalog-0171.title: Statue of Osorkon I
catalog-0171.author: Ancient Egyptian artisan
catalog-0171.background: This statue of an Egyptian pharaoh is displayed among works from the eastern Mediterranean, offering evidence of far-reaching regional exchange. Both the royal name and image assert his authority.
catalog-0171.look: Study the shape of the crown and torso, and compare this statue with sculptures from neighboring regions. It helps us imagine a crossroads where cultures met.

catalog-0172.title: Egyptian-Style Pectoral
catalog-0172.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0172.background: This ornament adapts the form of an Egyptian chest pendant, showing how visual motifs traveled across the eastern Mediterranean. Local imitation often sparked new regional craft traditions.
catalog-0172.look: Observe the symmetry of the motifs on left and right, and compare them with authentic Egyptian examples. Take note of the colors and materials as well.

catalog-0173.title: Golden Calf
catalog-0173.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0173.background: This small calf figure is finished in gold. Animals frequently served as symbols of both religious devotion and wealth, inviting us to consider ancient metallurgy and belief side by side.
catalog-0173.look: Notice the curve of the horns and back, and observe how the metal catches the light. Imagine the sacred or ceremonial setting in which such a small figurine might have been used.

catalog-0174.title: Duck-Shaped Small Box
catalog-0174.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0174.background: This small container takes the shape of a waterbird. Combining an everyday object with an animal form, it illustrates the playful spirit of eastern Mediterranean craftsmanship.
catalog-0174.look: See how the head connects seamlessly to the body, and spot where the lid sits. It reads simultaneously as a sculpted bird and a functional box.

catalog-0175.title: Ugarit Bowl with Hunting Motifs
catalog-0175.author: Ancient Ugaritic metalworker
catalog-0175.background: Hunting scenes are engraved around this bowl from Ugarit, a thriving hub of Mediterranean trade where artistic motifs from distant lands converged in fine metalwork.
catalog-0175.look: Follow the hunters and their prey in sequence, reading the story as it unfolds around the circle of the bowl. Pay close attention to the precision of the fine engraved lines.

catalog-0176.title: Box Lid Depicting a Goddess Nursing Goats
catalog-0176.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0176.background: This small box lid is carved with a scene linking a goddess and animals, imagery evoking abundance and nourishment. Even on a miniature scale, this ivory carving opens a window onto ancient belief.
catalog-0176.look: Observe the placement of the goddess and the goats, and check the depth of the relief carving. Picture this piece as the crowning lid of a complete container.

catalog-0177.title: Woman Holding a Child in a Cradle
catalog-0177.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0177.background: This figurine depicts a woman carrying a child. Alongside statues of kings and gods, intimate scenes of daily life have survived—making the ancient world feel remarkably close through this image of parent and child.
catalog-0177.look: Spot the tiny form of the child and follow the curve of the woman's arms. Notice how her posture shifts to support the weight.

catalog-0178.title: Figures Making Bread or Beer
catalog-0178.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0178.background: This small group sculpture shows figures gathered around a vessel. Scholars think it depicts either bread-making or beer-brewing, leaving room for interpretation as to the exact task.
catalog-0178.look: Count the figures and follow the movement of their hands, focusing on the container at the center. The group vividly evokes communal labor in antiquity.

catalog-0179.title: Model of a Boat with Figures
catalog-0179.author: Ancient Levantine artisan
catalog-0179.background: This miniature model portrays a boat and its passengers, reflecting a region where maritime trade and travel were vital. Reduced in scale from a real vessel, the model captures a story of seafaring life.
catalog-0179.look: Compare the size of the hull with the figures aboard, and see which way each passenger is facing. It is easy to picture them gliding across the water.

catalog-0180.title: Commode with Monkey Motifs
catalog-0180.author: 18th-century French cabinetmaker
catalog-0180.background: This courtly piece of furniture is decorated with playful monkey motifs. By adding whimsical ornament to a practical chest of drawers, furniture became a showcase for aristocratic taste.
catalog-0180.look: Search for the figures of the monkeys, and contrast the wooden surfaces with the gilt-bronze mounts. Notice how the lines of the drawers blend seamlessly into the decoration.

catalog-0181.title: Marie-Antoinette's Travel Case
catalog-0181.author: 18th-century French artisan
catalog-0181.background: This portable case was made for the queen's journeys, fitted out with a complete set of essential implements. It offers an intimate, concrete glimpse into daily life at the French court.
catalog-0181.look: Look at the interior compartments and trace the shape and placement of each tool. Compare its opulent materials with the cleverness of its portable design.

catalog-0182.title: Clock Depicting the Creation of the World
catalog-0182.author: 18th-century French clockmaker
catalog-0182.background: This timepiece pairs mechanical precision with a cosmic theme, uniting Enlightenment curiosity about science with decorative craftsmanship. It was designed as much to display its intricate mechanism as to tell time.
catalog-0182.look: Examine the dial alongside the sculptural figures surrounding it, and look for where mechanics meet sculpture. Imagine the entire ensemble in motion.

catalog-0183.title: Boat-Shaped Potpourri Vase
catalog-0183.author: 18th-century French ceramist
catalog-0183.background: This fragrance vessel borrows the silhouette of a ship, pushing porcelain into bold, sculptural complexity. It exemplifies both the technical mastery and playful spirit of the royal court.
catalog-0183.look: Pick out the bow and stern, and locate the pierced openings designed to release scent. Marvel at how fragile ceramic is transformed into the likeness of a vessel at sea.

catalog-0184.title: Pair of Vases with Ear-Shaped Handles
catalog-0184.author: 18th-century French ceramist
catalog-0184.background: These matching decorative vases feature handles that flare outward like ears. Designed as a pair, they brought symmetry and visual balance to courtly interiors.
catalog-0184.look: Compare the two silhouettes to see how closely they match, and follow the graceful curve of the handles. Look closely at the painted decoration to spot subtle variations.

catalog-0185.title: Commode with Japanese Lacquer
catalog-0185.author: 18th-century French cabinetmaker
catalog-0185.background: This French cabinet incorporates authentic Japanese lacquer panels. Materials from afar were prized and repurposed to suit European aristocratic taste, bringing techniques from distant worlds together in a single piece.
catalog-0185.look: Contrast the glossy lacquer panels with the metal mounts, and seek out the East Asian motifs. Reflect on the contrast between the European furniture form and its imported surface.

catalog-0186.title: Table Centerpiece
catalog-0186.author: 18th-century French artisan
catalog-0186.background: Crafted to adorn the center of a dining table, this piece set the social stage around which guests gathered for meals. Such elaborate ornament transformed dining into a theatrical experience.
catalog-0186.look: Observe how the design spreads outward from the center to each side, and consider what items it could hold. It helps you envision the grand scale of the banquet table.

catalog-0187.title: Tureen and Underplate
catalog-0187.author: 18th-century French artisan
catalog-0187.background: This matching tureen and stand were used to present and serve dishes at table. Their forms and ornament reflect courtly etiquette, elevating tableware into independent works of decorative art.
catalog-0187.look: Compare the decoration on the lid with that on the underplate, and notice the shaping of the handles. Picture the graceful gestures of serving from this ensemble.

catalog-0188.title: Tapestry of the Story of Don Quixote
catalog-0188.author: 18th-century French tapestry weaver
catalog-0188.background: Woven after Cervantes's famous novel, this tapestry both warmed and decorated the wall while narrating an episode from the story—seamlessly uniting literature and interior design.
catalog-0188.look: Locate the characters within the scene, and look closely at how transitions of color are built from woven threads. Then step back a little to take in the full composition.

catalog-0189.title: Chair from the Comte d'Artois's Turkish Cabinet
catalog-0189.author: 18th-century French cabinetmaker
catalog-0189.background: Made for an exotic-themed room, this chair reflects eighteenth-century France's imaginative vision of Turkish style. Even seating was designed to help stage the atmosphere of the entire interior.
catalog-0189.look: Observe the distinctive contour of the backrest, and compare the upholstery with the carved wooden frame. Imagine the role this chair played within the room as a whole.

catalog-0190.title: Snuffbox with a Portrait of Louis XV
catalog-0190.author: 18th-century French goldsmith
catalog-0190.background: This small box conceals a portrait of the king on the inside of its lid. Tucking a royal likeness into a personal accessory expressed political allegiance and intimacy—a miniature gem of courtly craftsmanship.
catalog-0190.look: Compare the exterior with the interior, and note the clever conceit of the hidden portrait. Held in the palm of the hand, the box showcases remarkable goldsmithing skill.

catalog-0191.title: Statue of a Naiad
catalog-0191.author: 18th-century French sculptor
catalog-0191.background: This decorative sculpture represents a water nymph from classical mythology, bringing poetic narrative into palace rooms or gardens by personifying the elemental force of water.
catalog-0191.look: Follow the flowing lines of her hair and drapery, and look for attributes suggesting water. Consider how the figure interacts with the surrounding space.

cheat.title: The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds
cheat.author: Georges de La Tour
cheat.background: This masterpiece is by Georges de La Tour, who pioneered a distinctive world of light and shadow in seventeenth-century France. Set in crisp daylight, it stages a thrilling psychological drama: a naive, wealthy young man is about to be thoroughly duped by three conspiring swindlers.
cheat.look: Follow the gazes of the four figures. The woman in the center exchanges a knowing glance with the maidservant pouring wine, while the man on the far left reaches behind his back to pull out a hidden ace of diamonds. Only the young man on the right, absorbed in his hand of cards, remains completely blind to the trap closing around him.

bather.title: The Valpinçon Bather
bather.author: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres
bather.background: Painted when Ingres was twenty-eight during his studies in Rome, this is his first great masterpiece of the female nude. The pure contour of the woman seen from behind and the soft, nearly shadowless light create a timeless stillness reminiscent of ancient sculpture.
bather.look: Savor the contrasting textures of the smooth skin along her back, the green curtain draped on the left, and the crisp white sheet at her feet. Ingres remained captivated by this rear view for the rest of his life—fifty-four years later, he placed her once again at the center of his late masterpiece, The Turkish Bath.

clubfoot.title: The Clubfoot
clubfoot.author: Jusepe de Ribera
clubfoot.background: Painted in Naples in 1642 by the Spanish master Jusepe de Ribera, this deeply moving work celebrates human dignity. A poor boy with a deformed right foot stands proudly with a crutch slung over his shoulder, showing neither self-pity nor sorrow, but a radiant smile.
clubfoot.look: The small slip of paper in the boy's left hand bears a Latin inscription asking for alms for the love of God. Yet Ribera paints him from the same low vantage point reserved for royal and aristocratic portraits, silhouetted against an open blue sky with unshakable pride and vitality.
